task: Write a comprehensive, publication-ready academic manuscript on the S.U.R.E. (Aquaculture Welfare Integration) system: an autonomous sturgeon welfare monitoring system in Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) using Edge-AI (YOLOv11s + ByteTrack), a dual-layer LLM + deterministic rule engine safety architecture, RAG-enhanced retrieval (pgvector + e5-small), and PSI-gated MLOps drift detection. The system is already implemented, deployed, and tested; the paper must contextualize the dual-layer AI safety approach within the precision aquaculture literature and argue it solves LLM unreliability in safety-critical industrial deployments.

changes: Fixed 3 figure rendering bugs: fig2 (F1-argmax annotation collided with markers), fig3 (title/pt-cpu overlap, an out-of-range annotation distorted the y-axis and drew a line through the 10^1 tick label and the x-axis title, onnx/torchscript labels stacked illegibly since their data points nearly coincide), fig4/doc-Figure-5 (PSI curves rode over the SIGNIFICANT/MODERATE threshold-line labels). All fixed in figures/make_figures.py with explicit ylim/xlim, white text bboxes, and diverging leader-line arrows for the near-coincident onnx/torchscript points; verified by rendering each figure to PNG and visually inspecting before/after.

Corrected a paper-wide factual overclaim about deployment status: the manuscript previously implied S.U.R.E. is a live, field-deployed system. Per the actual authors: no test used real physical sensors or an operating RAS facility (no such sensor hardware exists at all); sensor readings used throughout are synthetically generated, not recorded; the 510-image vision dataset IS real (camera footage of the physical rig, hand-labeled) but intentionally small, with expansion planned; the team did not enter TEKNOFEST (the competition S.U.R.E. was built for) and did not pass its preliminary evaluation round; the actual purpose of the work is a feasibility/resource-management demonstration (testing whether the multi-component pipeline's memory/compute footprint is viable on edge hardware), not a field validation of decision accuracy.

Reworded 'deployed'/'production'/'real-world' language across abstract, introduction, background, system_architecture, experimental_setup, results, discussion, known_limitations, conclusion, related_work, and acknowledgements sections -- distinguishing legitimate 'configured parameter value' references (kept) from live-field-operation implications (corrected to 'implemented'/'offline, bench-level evaluation').
